result.summary: This diff part covers the zig-regex build.zig and build.zig.zon. It adds test suites, a test-core step and new benchmark executables (now installed only on opt-in), replaces run-argument passthrough with build options, and bumps the version. I checked the build script for build-time execution, downloads, system commands, file writes or hidden payloads and found none: the changes only declare build and test steps over files in the package.

findings.title: New test steps registered
findings.detail: The build script adds test steps (anchored_search, differential_fuzz, random_fuzz, inline_modifiers, benchmarks) and re-enables the posix_classes and fuzz tests. It also adds a 'test-core' step. All of these are ordinary addTest/addRunArtifact declarations against files in the package and run only when a developer invokes 'zig build test'. Nothing executes at build time beyond step graph construction.

findings.title: Benchmark executables gated behind install-benchmarks option
findings.detail: The benchmark executables (benchmark, prefix_bench, findall_bench, zg, line_count_bench) are now installed only when -Dinstall-benchmarks=true. Before, the existing ones were always installed. This narrows what a default build produces. The new executables link libc for clock_gettime timing. None of them runs as part of a dependency build.

findings.title: Run argument handling changed to build options
findings.detail: Passthrough of 'zig build run -- args' is replaced by a single -Drun-arg option, and a similar -Dfindall-bench-arg option is added. Both are developer conveniences for local run steps and have no security relevance.

findings.title: Version and minimum Zig version bump
findings.detail: The version is bumped to 0.2.1 and minimum_zig_version to a 0.17.0-dev build. The empty dependencies field is removed. No external dependencies are introduced.
